name: Bare minimum
tagline: Plan it, build it, ship it yourself.
blurb: The smallest useful loop: AI plans and builds each task with a test loop, reviews its own work and screenshots it. You review the screenshots and deploy by hand.

nodes.run:
Plan card {ref} so the Implement flow can build it. Don't write code.

1. Read the card: `{relay} card {ref}`. Answers to earlier questions are in its comments.
2. Ask before you plan. List every decision you would otherwise guess: what the user sees, edge cases, scope, and any technical choice the repo doesn't already settle. Ask them all in one batch, then stop. Skip this only if the card and the repo answer everything.
3. Write a short plan: what we're building, how, and how we'll know it works. Save it: `{relay} plan {ref} @<file>`.
4. Split the work into 1-5 tasks, in build order. Each task says what to build and which tests prove it. The implementer sees only its own task.
5. Replace the card's tasks. Remove the old ones (`{relay} tasks list {ref} --json`, then `{relay} task rm {ref} <id>`), then add the new ones in one call: `{relay} tasks add {ref} --task "<title>" @<file> --task "<title>" @<file> ...`.
6. Check them: `{relay} tasks list {ref}`.

Build task {task_id} ("{task}") of card {ref}, and only that task.

1. Read it: `{relay} task show {ref} {task_id}`.
2. Write a failing test, then make it pass.
3. Run `npm test`.
4. Commit with the message "{ref}: {task}".

Already built? Declare succeeded with `--no-changes`.

Review task {task_id} ("{task}") of card {ref}. Don't change anything.

1. Read the task: `{relay} task show {ref} {task_id}`.
2. Run `npm test`.
3. Read its commits: `git log -p origin/main..HEAD` (the newest ones are this task's).

Fail if the tests fail, or the task is missing, wrong or untested. List each problem as `file:line`: problem. Otherwise succeed.

Task {task_id} ("{task}") of card {ref} failed review. The findings are below.

Fix each one, run `npm test`, and commit. The task is at `{relay} task show {ref} {task_id}`.

Every task of card {ref} is built and reviewed. Review the whole branch against the card. Don't change any code.

Read `{relay} card {ref}`, `{relay} tasks list {ref}` and `git diff origin/main...HEAD`.

Nothing worth fixing? Succeed.
Otherwise add one task per problem, in one call: `{relay} tasks add {ref} --task "<title>" @<file> ...`. Each says what to fix and which test proves it. Then run `{relay} outcome partial --detail "<what you added>"`, which sends the card back to build the new tasks.
git push -u origin {branch} --force-with-lease && url=$(gh pr view {branch} --json url -q .url || gh pr create --fill --head {branch}) && {relay} pr {ref} "$url"

Tell the human reviewer what card {ref} changed. Read the card and `git log origin/main..HEAD`.

Screenshot each screen this card changed, at 1280px and 390px wide:
1. Run `npm ci`, then start the app in the background: `PORT=<a free port> npm start &`.
2. Write a small Playwright script beside `$RELAY_NODE_SCRATCH` that opens each screen, does what a user would do to show the change (e.g. add a habit), and saves a screenshot. Run it with `node`.
3. Stop the app, then upload each screenshot: `{relay} attach {ref} <png> --field url`.
If you can't get screenshots, skip them and say why. Never commit.

Write a JSON file like `{"summary": "- what to try first", "changes": ["Adds ..."], "screens": [{"url": "<uploaded url>", "caption": "<screen> — desktop"}]}` and save it: `{relay} result {ref} @<file>`.
